items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Neon gains momentum ahead of OpenAI, data shows
items.summary: Logan Kilpatrick, Google (GOOG) AI Studio and Gemini API Product Lead, joins Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa–as data shows Google's Gemini 4 Neon gaining momentum with developers–to discuss how the company will focus on competing against Chinese open-source models.

items.title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia: Long or short accountability?
items.summary:
Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia's board unanimously reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and what the White House's involvement says about accountability in corporate America, whether the government has effectively put a floor under the AI trade, and Anthropic falling as options on the stock begin trading for the first time.

The panel, with Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, debates where everyone sits on a one-to-five bullishness scale, whether this is a stock picker's market or a CapEx bubble that precedes a secular bear, the risk of a politically driven slowdown in data center construction, and OpenAI's chief scientist calling for a speed limit on AI development, including whether an FDA-style regulator is the right model for AI.

items.title: Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, stock soars; Anthropic slides
items.summary: The 8:30 team is joined by Roundhill Investments Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit to discuss why washed-out sentiment doesn't mean a fundamental bottom, his $50-to-$250 bull-bear range on Anthropic, and how to handicap the "Jensen premium" coming back into Nvidia. Deirdre Bosa Live host Deirdre Bosa also joins to break down Silicon Valley's reaction to Huang's return and what it means for the AI trade.

items.title: Jensen Huang is back: Does Washington have a seat in the boardroom?
items.summary: As Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang and investors add a trillion dollars to the stock, Deirdre Bosa dives into the White House's role in his return and asks General Catalyst's Madhu Namburi, who spent 25 years advising tech boards at J.P.
